sections.content:
44,190 people

were counted on the census as "childminders" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Childminders provide day-to-day care of children in their own homes, and supervise and participate in their play, educational and other activities.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "childminders" there were more women than men (95.7% compared with 4.3%).

This means "childminders" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 4.3% and women made up 95.7% of "childminders"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "childminders" included:

  • school midday and crossing patrol occupations
  • medical secretaries
  • registered community nurses

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 40 to 44 years. Of the whole working population 10.9% were aged 40 to 44 years. For people working as "childminders", 14.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "childminders" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "childminders" included:

  • teaching assistants
  • careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists
  • florists

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "childminders" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of women than men with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "childminders" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "childminders", 9.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (60.9% compared with 39.1%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (78.2%) than an employee (21.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
